source.title: Scaling Laws for Task-Specific LLM Distillation
source.authors: Lavinia Ghita; Dhruv Desai; Ioana Boier

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no truncation or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies the parameter count of pruned-and-distilled students and measures downstream task and benchmark performance. This is a different setup from pretraining scaling laws, but it bears on V6's downstream-performance-versus-scale claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream metrics across pruning schedules and model sizes. Its dataset-size experiments vary training examples at fixed 50% student size, not training tokens for pretraining, and are not results on held-out pretraining loss. It does not fit or report the original parameter/token/compute power laws or a compute-optimal allocation. Referenced scaling-law findings are not treated as this study's results.
record.test_reason: Despite its title, the study fits no power law. Its size axis is the compression ratio of pruned-and-distilled students of one pretrained teacher (Qwen3-32B), not pretraining scale. Training data also doubles at each iterative step, so student size is confounded with data budget. No row measures held-out pretraining loss, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation or architecture shape. The downstream results (in-domain Macro F1, MMLU) concern post-hoc compression, a different kind of system from the scaled pretrained LMs V6 names. They are recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test of V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress three further points. Supervision format is the key driver of the task-vs-general-knowledge tradeoff, with blended CoT actively recovering general knowledge lost to pruning. Training-induced distribution shift accounts for roughly twice the gap that compression to 16% introduces. In-domain quality degrades predictably while general-knowledge benchmarks collapse much earlier.
record.recipe_differences: This is task-specific pruning and distillation of a pretrained Qwen3-32B teacher, evaluated on classification and general-knowledge benchmarks; it does not use the original held-out pretraining-loss measurement or fit the original scaling-law forms.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with pruning schedule and step, supervision format, distillation method, dataset size, and evaluation metric. Intermediate Macro F1 varies sharply by schedule; the paper also reports different general-knowledge retention across methods.

fits_no_version.finding: Under iterative blended-CoT KD with a graduated data budget, in-domain Macro F1 is nearly flat from 79% (0.7724) to 16% (0.7759) of teacher size. It shows transient collapses, e.g. polynomial Step 2 at 0.1041, which the authors attribute to label-formatting failures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-specific performance of pruned-and-distilled students is largely insensitive to compression ratio down to ~16% when distillation data scale with compression steps.

fits_no_version.finding: MMLU of distilled students falls steeply with compression (e.g. uniform 76.46 at 79% to 26.93 at 16%), reaching near random at 16%. MMLU-Pro falls similarly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: General-knowledge benchmarks degrade much faster than in-domain task quality under structured pruning plus domain distillation.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed 50% student, the methods scale differently with dataset size. Blended CoT KD Macro F1 improves across 3.125k to 400k examples. Blended-LoRA NLL/Brier worsens after an early optimum. Direct-label KD is non-monotonic (Figures 4-5, not in rows).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data scaling of distilled students depends on supervision format and update scope, with no single monotone trend.

record.problems: One dense teacher and one synthetic financial classification task; the principal parameter-size sweep changes model size through pruning and distillation rather than pretraining scale. Results are means across three seeds, but no numerical uncertainty intervals are reported in the text. Task-specific metrics and benchmark scores are not held-out pretraining loss, and the study does not fit power laws or test extrapolation.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted detailed data-size-scaling results at fixed 50% student size, general-knowledge curves for those runs, and intermediate-step MMLU-Pro values in Table 3; these vary data/supervision or add benchmark points but do not add a separate test of the original pretraining-loss law. Table 3 MMLU-Pro Step-1 through Step-3 values were also omitted to keep the extracted rows focused on size endpoints and the reported additional compression step.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute; no power-law fit at all.
Extrapolation from small to large runs.
Shape effects on pretraining loss at fixed parameter count. The pruning depth/width allocation remarks (Appendix A) concern recoverability after distillation, not pretraining loss.
Power-law form in fine-tuning/distillation regimes. Data-size curves at fixed 50% student are reported, but no power law is fitted.
Downstream performance vs pretraining scale or pretraining loss; only compression ratio of one teacher is varied.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup choices; no exponents are fitted.

record.verdict_notes: The title's 'scaling laws' are empirical trend curves; no functional form or exponent is fitted. The reader's 'tests/T2' with V6 labels is overturned. Student size is set by pruning a single pretrained model and is confounded with the doubling data budget per step. The in-domain ceiling is set by the teacher's own labels. Values in all rows were checked against Table 3 and Section 5.2 and match.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law form and several-orders-of-magnitude range.
Extrapolation from small pretraining runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its dependence on compute.
Architecture-shape effects on held-out pretraining loss at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes. The study's task-specific distillation results do not fit or test that form.
Performance versus pretraining loss, pretraining-scale extrapolation, and downstream tasks beyond the tested financial classification and MMLU benchmarks.
Dependence of fitted original-law exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MMLU across the reported compression sizes and schedules, especially the broad decline toward the 16% target
reader_labels.reason: MMLU scores generally fall as student size is reduced, consistent with a downstream benchmark tracking scale in this tested compression setting; see R26-R49.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Iterative task-classification performance across pruning schedules and intermediate checkpoints
reader_labels.reason: Macro F1 depends on the compression path and is not uniformly monotonic; the polynomial Step-2 collapse is followed by recovery, and the 16% endpoint differs by schedule. See R1-R25.
